subject: Interim update and guidance — ClearWave chat stream slowdown (edge shard recovery)
messages:
From: Jordan Ricks <jordan.ricks@clearwave.io>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: ClearWave Platform <platform@clearwave.io>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Live Chat — sudden streaming stalls this morning

Hi Naomi,

We're seeing our Live Support chat streaming stall and very high tail latency starting around 08:00 PST. Messages either arrive in large batches ~30–60s after they are typed, or the stream drops and client reconnects without any tokens. This hit about 20% of sessions and is causing a degraded experience for customers.

Attached is a short curl trace and the client-side logs we captured (small snippet). Can you confirm if there is an ongoing incident on your side and any immediate workarounds we should apply?

What we need:
- A short list of safe, low-risk client changes we can apply now (no schema changes)
- ETA for when you'll have a mitigation in place

Thanks — this is high priority for us.

Jordan
Senior SRE, ClearWave
[Attachment: clearwave-curl-trace.txt]
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ricks <jordan.ricks@clearwave.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 08:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Live Chat — sudden streaming stalls this morning

Hi Jordan — thanks for the heads up and the logs. We're actively investigating; heading in with both Prod and Edge teams. Immediate guidance you can apply (no schema or model change required):

Client-side mitigations (ship now):
- Reduce concurrent streaming connections per user to 1 (we've seen clients open 2–4).
- If you use parallel prompt generation for multi-agent flows, fallback to serialized requests for the live channel.
- Enable short reconnect logic with token-resume: on disconnect, resume stream requesting last-known sequence token (we'll continue the prefix KV).
- If interruption persists, switch to the non-streaming /generate endpoint for that session and poll at 1–2s. This increases cost slightly but avoids UI stalls.
- Lower your max_token_buffer to 512 for chat windows with >4 turns to reduce per-request working set.

These changes are safe and reversible. We'll keep you updated on root cause and platform mitigations. I've looped in our support (Marissa) and infra lead (Vivek). Also attaching a short diagnostic form if you can fill remaining session ids/region info.

Best,
Naomi
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: diagnostic-request-form.pdf]
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 08:35:00 -0800
Subject: FW: Live Chat — sudden streaming stalls this morning

Team — forwarding ClearWave's report. Symptoms: intermittent high tail latency and stream drops affecting ~20% of sessions beginning ~08:00 PST. A few notes:

- Affected routes: /v1/chat/stream on region us-west-2; customer uses our hosted API with edge shard routing.
- Client observed large batching of tokens or silent disconnects.
- They provided curl trace and session ids.

Can infra/edge please:
1) Confirm whether any rolling jobs, shard compaction, or controller GC events occurred in us-west-2 between 07:45–08:15 PST.
2) Provide last 1h of edge shard metrics (queue length, active streams, kernel backlog) and any OOMs.
3) If this is a resource exhaustion / head-of-line blocking issue, please propose immediate mitigation (e.g., rolling restart of a subset, increase shard count, adjust backpressure thresholds) we can communicate to the customer.

Marissa — please keep ClearWave updated with the client workarounds Naomi posted; offer temporary credits if SLA impacted.

Thanks,
Naomi
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 10:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FW: Live Chat — sudden streaming stalls this morning

Quick postmortem note and immediate actions taken (ops):

What we saw:
- Root cause: concurrency regression in edge shard controller that allowed inflight streaming sessions to accumulate KV-cache references without timely eviction (regression introduced in rwinf-2026.10.30.02). This caused head-of-line blocking and increased inference latency under certain request size distributions.
- Impact window: 07:50–09:05 PST. Peak affected traffic: ~22% of streams in us-west-2.

Immediate mitigations executed (08:50–09:00 PST):
- Rolled a targeted restart of 30% of edge shard group us-west-2 (staggered 20s intervals) to break stuck sessions.
- Deployed a hotfix rwinf-2026.11.12.01 that adds faster KV eviction and a protective semaphore around controller compaction.
- Temporarily lowered streaming concurrency limit at the shard-proxy layer from 8 to 4 to reduce queue head-of-line risk.

Evidence & artifacts: attached compressed logs for the impacted shard group and the hotfix diff.

Next steps:
- Full regression patch and integration tests scheduled for the 2026-11-19 release window.
- We'll add a canary for KV eviction metrics and a synthetic streaming workload to catch similar regressions.
- Postmortem doc with timeline + RCA will follow tomorrow; we'll include suggested long-term config changes for customer routing.

Attachments: edge-shard-logs-20261112.tar.gz, hotfix-rwinf-2026.11.12.01.diff

Marcus
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ricks <jordan.ricks@clearwave.io>, ClearWave Platform <platform@clearwave.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 18:45:00 -0800
Subject: Summary & next steps — ClearWave streaming incident (11/12)

Hi Jordan — thanks again for your patience today. Below is a concise summary for your ops and product teams, plus recommended actions and our follow-up commitments.

What happened (brief):
- Between ~07:50–09:05 PST on 2026-11-12, a regression in our edge shard controller caused accumulation of KV-cache references which produced head-of-line blocking on streaming routes. ~22% of streams in us-west-2 saw elevated tail latency or disconnects.

Short-term actions you can take (recommended order):
1) Implement the client-side mitigations from our 08:28 note (reduce concurrency to 1 per user on live channels; enable reconnect-with-resume; lower max_token_buffer to 512).
2) If you're using parallel agent flows for a single user session, switch that channel to serialized requests for the next 48h to avoid compounding the effect.
3) As a last resort, for any live chat session that must be uninterrupted, call the non-stream /generate endpoint and poll at 1–2s (we will prioritize capacity for these calls temporarily).

What we did for you:
- Targeted rolling restart of 30% of the us-west-2 edge shard group; hotfix rwinf-2026.11.12.01 rolled to production; lowered shard-proxy concurrency temporarily.
- We have provisionally prioritized ClearWave traffic for non-stream fallback routes while you decide whether to switch.

Commitments & timeline:
- Full regression patch and additional tests: ETA 2026-11-19.
- Canary and synthetic workload checks: next 48–72 hours.
- Formal postmortem with timeline, RCA, and long-term mitigations: delivered by EOD 2026-11-13 (tomorrow).

Credits & next steps:
- We recognize the impact to your live support experience. Marissa will open a billing credit request and propose a one-time operational credit to compensate for affected sessions.
- Please send any additional session ids or traces to support@redwood.ai (or reply to this thread) and we'll attach them to the incident.

Again apologies for the disruption — we know this affects your customer experience and are treating this as a Sev-2 incident with priority remediation. I'll follow up with the full postmortem tomorrow and a link to the incident page.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
[Related link: https://status.redwood.ai/incident/2026-11-12-edge-shard-01]
